newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan seen merging state trading houses.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan seen merging state trading houses.

text.p: Pakistan's caretaker government is likely to merge its three major commodity trading houses to cut spending and subsidies, officials said on Monday.
The move would be in line with sweeping reform plans set out on Saturday by Shahid Javed Burki, finance and economic affairs adviser to interim Prime Minister Meraj Khalid.

Burki took a 90-day leave of absence from the World Bank, where he is a vice-president, after President Farooq Leghari, who sacked Benazir Bhutto's government on Tuesday, asked him to take charge of the Finance Ministry.

"With Burki leading the finance ministry, we expect the government to seriously look into this proposal, originally submitted by the World Bank itself," said an official of the state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP).

The official said the government was considering merging the TCP with the Rice Export Corporation (RECP) and the Cotton Export Corporation (CEC) as part of a drive to reduce expenditure and duplication.

He said all three organisations had incurred substantial losses in recent years, although he said the TCP had turned a profit in fiscal 1995/96 (July-June) when it imported sugar and vegetable oil, and exported rice, fruit and clinker.

Successive cotton crop failures from 1993 to 1995 had made the CEC virtually redundant, the official said. The corporation had actually been asked to import cotton from central Asian states during that period, he added.

Even when Pakistan enjoyed a bumper crop in 1995/96, the CEC had been unable to export a single bale of cotton. After a ban on cotton exports was lifted, private dealers exported all the estimated 1.8 million bales Pakistan sold in that year.
Private rice exporters have frequently demanded that the government wind up RECP.
Javed Islam Agha, a former president of the private Rice Exporters Association of Pakistan, said exporters would be much better off and could market products more easily without RECP.

The TCP official said that apart from the trading corporations, the government was also considering scrapping the Pakistan Agriculture Storage and Services Corporation, the Punjab Agriculture Development and Supplies Corporation, the Punjab Seed Corporation and National Fertilizer Marketing Ltd.
The official said most of these bodies were chronic loss-makers that survived on heavy government subsidies.
"A single organisation for supporting farm prices and a single organisation for exporting these commodities is probably on the mind of the World Bank vice-president," he said.
